entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Ngawang Namgyal (1512-1544) was the prince of the Rinpungpa dynasty that dominated the Tsang region in West Central Tibet between 1435 and 1565.

As the ruler of this powerful dynasty, Ngawang Namgyal played a crucial role in the cultural and religious landscape of Tibet, patronizing the Karma Kagyu school, a prominent school within the Tibetan Buddhist tradition. His reign was marked by significant political and economic changes, including the expansion of the Rinpungpa empire and the establishment of a strong monastic institution.

Ngawang Namgyal's legacy extends beyond his own reign, as he set the stage for the eventual decline of the Rinpungpa dynasty and paved the way for the rise of other Tibetan dynasties. His patronage of the Karma Kagyu school also had a lasting impact on Tibetan Buddhism, shaping the development of the school's teachings and practices.

The exact dates of Ngawang Namgyal's birth and death are unknown, adding to the enigmatic nature of his historical figure.
